title: Working on a narrative RPG set in a city slowly drowning
author: Natural-Shirt-1463
selftext:
Here's the protagonist's apartment

I'm developing The Drowned Republic, a narrative RPG inspired by Disco Elysium.

The game takes place in Vesper, a city divided by elevation and social class. The wealthy live comfortably on dry, elevated ground, while the poorest residents survive in partially flooded neighborhoods, relying on homemade gasoline-powered pumps to keep their homes habitable.

You play as Xander Voss, a sarcastic, 34-year-old floodgate operator who dreams of escaping the lower districts.

The game begins with Xander waking up to find his apartment flooded because his pump ran out of gasoline. You can borrow fuel from a neighbor, buy it, or steal it, with different outcomes depending on your character's skills and choices.

This screenshot shows his apartment. It's still an early prototype, but I'm aiming for a hand-painted, atmospheric RPG focused on dialogue, exploration, and meaningful consequences.

Would love some feedback on the art direction and premise!

comments.author: maddix_cummings
comments.body:
Did you overuse ChatGPT for texture generation? It's got its texture and shadow accentuation all over the place, that's not how any of these materials would normally look like, much less slowly decaying in water. I won't comment on the rest though there's a lot to say but the biggest issue is the water. 

Why is the water blue? Is there lore to it? Have you ever seen flooded rooms? I'd get it if there was sediment or if the flood was recent but here it's blue and almost opaque (can't see protagonist's feet). And the backdrop is dark but the window has a bright sky? Overall it's very sloppy, I'd recommend you set a clear moodboard up and do a pass to remove accentuation on your textures.

replies.author: Natural-Shirt-1463
replies.body:
It's a stylized, hand-painted game, not a photorealistic flood simulation. The water is blue-grey because of the lighting and color palette, not because it needs some special lore explanation. And a brighter sky outside a dark interior isn't exactly unrealistic.

That said, I agree the water could use better transparency and the textures need refinement. It's an early prototype, after all. I appreciate actionable feedback, but not every artistic choice needs to replicate real-world materials perfectly.

replies.author: maddix_cummings
replies.body:
Stylization does not defeat in world logic. Saying opaque blue water is fine with absolutely no explanation is just being incoherent. Which is fine, sure. But there's a reason why most games do not portray water as opaque and why games that choose a rendering style that is as realistic (though stylized realism) usually stick to coherence. 

The sky is not brighter than the dark INTERIOR, your backdrop is DARK as in night  time. Which would indicate to any player that it is not bright outside. That is basic coherence. And with AI I don't get why you wouldn't just... generate a sunny one for day time? A backdrop is what is outside of your play area in this case if you will. 

I have never said every artistic choice needs to replicate real-world materials perfectly, leave it to photorealistic PBR workflow. I am saying it is: 1. Not coherent. 2. Bad UX. If you except to post stuff and be touchy about feedback, I don't understand what you're looking for here. Praise about it?

replies.author: darkoblivion000
replies.body:
So the problem with OPs original as well as this one, is that the image actually has too much detail. Imagegen often adds additional detail that doesn’t have to be there to make it “high quality” but in reality makes it very noisy and over detailed AI look to the human eye.

Also inconsistencies like look at the candle reflection on the water. Why does it bend around the table? First the table it’s sitting on and then bends around the bed and then bends around again the other table

Imagegen produces more and more visual inconsistencies the more detailed a scene is. It is difficult to consistently produce multiple scenes with everything visually right, but I have found success in many cases asking it to denoise. Remove textures from surfaces decrease small particles, reduce grittiness feeling, and make it more of a painted feel

If I avoid some of that prompting it will produce very noisy textures and I notice each iteration it gets more and more grainy as it keeps trying to add more detail and then it becomes extremely sloppy
